analysis: The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md. The visible patch excerpt changes the DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_DEADLINE_MODE row (head lines 413-414): the default moves from `off` to `enforce`, and any value other than `off` now enforces. The patch excerpt is truncated, and neither supplied text unit covers lines 413-414 (the base unit starts at 520 and the head unit ends at 353). I could not see the full new row or any other hunks, so I did not inspect the PrefillDeadlineMode.swift code that the row cites. Assessment: this is documentation only, with no code, key, attestation, authorization or encryption change. The documented default flip would be fail-closed for admission (an availability/scheduling control), and unrecognized values enforce rather than disable. I did not find an impact on A-001, A-003, A-015/A-016, TB-002 or TB-011. The surrounding text in both units is unchanged context (GLM qualification, endpoint resumption/logout, App Attest worker flags, SSD prefix cache settings, model cache location). Its statements stay consistent with the threat model: worker flags use exact `1`, endpoint-resumption creates no local trust, and logout is local-only without issuer metadata. The SSD prefix cache section (base lines 587-619) matches T-041: 1800 s max TTL, an affirmative-opt-in DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE, and debug key file restrictions. The base unit shows no loosening of the TTL or the cache gate. Remaining question for integration: confirm that PrefillDeadlineMode.resolve in the source tree actually defaults to enforce, so the docs do not drift from behavior. This is a doc-accuracy question, not a vulnerability.
